slot.brief: find the complete general solution of a trigonometric equation reducible to a single function via factorisation or double-angle formulae

stem: The general solution of \(\cos x + \cos 3x = \cos 2x\) is
working:
Using sum-to-product: \(\cos x + \cos 3x = 2\cos 2x \cos x\).
The equation becomes \(2\cos 2x \cos x = \cos 2x\).
Rearrange: \(\cos 2x(2\cos x - 1) = 0\).
Hence \(\cos 2x = 0\) or \(\cos x = \frac12\).
\(\cos 2x = 0 \Rightarrow 2x = \frac{(2n+1)\pi}{2} \Rightarrow x = \frac{(2n+1)\pi}{4}\).
\(\cos x = \frac12 \Rightarrow x = 2n\pi \pm \frac{\pi}{3}\).
solution:
Using $
\cos x+\cos 3x=2\cos 2x\cos x$, the equation becomes
$$\cos 2x(2\cos x-1)=0.\]
Thus $\cos 2x=0$ gives $x=\frac{(2n+1)\pi}{4}$, while $\cos x=\frac12$ gives $x=2n\pi\pm\frac{\pi}{3}$, $n\in\mathbb Z$.
